reason: The skin cell needs to copy its DNA before it can divide, and the building blocks are shown arriving at that cell.
expectation: The cell will copy its DNA in preparation for division.

effect: The chromosomes have been copied, so the next step is to separate them for cell division.
reaction: The paired chromatids make the copying result clear.
reason: The spindle machinery is positioned to separate the copied chromosomes.
expectation: The sister chromatids will be separated toward opposite poles of the cell.

effect: The copied chromosomes are now separated into two matching sets, but the cell still has one shared interior.
reaction: The result makes the distinction between chromosome separation and cell division clear.
reason: The division ring is positioned to split the cell after its chromosomes separate.

choice.combine: Skin cell with separated chromosome sets

expectation: The ring will constrict and divide the cell into two cells.

effect: The skin cell has divided into two daughter cells, showing how basal cell division contributes to skin renewal.
reaction: The pinching sequence clearly connects the division ring to the two new cells.
reason: The new skin cells can now contribute to renewal in the same body.
expectation: The new cells will be incorporated into the body's skin renewal.

effect: The new cells are now connected to skin renewal in the same body; blood and bone renewal remain.
reaction: The basal cells and shedding surface make the ongoing replacement visible.
reason: Erythropoietin is shown carrying a kidney signal to the marrow precursors, suggesting it supports red-cell production.
expectation: The signal will stimulate the precursors to produce new red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal promotes maturation of red-cell precursors; the developing cells can now contribute to blood renewal.
reaction: The low-oxygen cue clarifies why the kidney sends the signal.
reason: The developing red cells belong in the same body that is renewing its skin.
expectation: The body will gain a renewed supply of red blood cells.

effect: The body now shows red cells entering the blood from marrow; bone renewal remains.
reaction: The kidney-to-marrow connection makes blood renewal feel connected to the rest of the body.
reason: The bone-removing and bone-forming cells are shown working on the same patch of bone, suggesting a remodeling sequence.
expectation: The cells will remove old bone matrix and replace it with new matrix.

effect: Bone removal happens within the body first; the bone-forming cells appear to be the next step.
reaction: I was surprised the two cell types did not combine directly, but the feedback made the sequence clear.
reason: The bone-forming cells can fill the patch where old bone was removed.
expectation: The cells will deposit new bone matrix in the remodeled patch.

effect: Bone-forming cells rebuilt the patch, completing the model of skin, blood and bone renewal in the same body.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the three renewal processes brought together in the person raising an arm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes and then dividing the cell made two distinct stages of skin-cell renewal clear. The descriptions showed why each daughter cell receives a complete set.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the new skin cells to the body felt fairly predictable after the division sequence, though it connected the close-up to the whole body.

surprise.text: I expected the bone-removing and bone-forming cells to combine directly. The feedback instead showed bone removal in the body before rebuilding.

arbitrary.text: The need to add the two bone cell types separately was not obvious from their descriptions, which showed them working on the same patch. The resulting sequence did give the separation a purpose.

continue.text: I would consider continuing if another chapter offered a similarly concrete connection between cell activity and the whole body. The renewal sequences were clear, although some assembly steps were predictable.
